title: git probe on Git for Windows
proves: rev-parse --git-path output with a drive letter (C:/...) and from a linked worktree parses; ls-tree -r -z with a project prefix returns the right paths; symlink entries (mode 120000) are filtered; cat-file --batch frames binary content correctly; reflog subjects parse.
does_not_prove: Any Git build other than Git for Windows, or colocated jj.

title: the gate during a real git switch of a 4,000-file tree
proves: The controller reports the gate closed for every real marker git creates during a switch of a large tree, and releases it afterward (six switches). The skip-never-delete behavior for an unreadable file is a hub behavior, covered by a5.
does_not_prove: Antivirus or OneDrive interplay, or timings on a cold cache.

title: core.autocrlf=true: classifier and arrival comparisons
proves: A CRLF-checked-out file compares equal to its blob content after normalization, through the classifier and the arrival comparison, for text; binaries compare by bytes.
does_not_prove: .gitattributes filters (LFS, ident), or the CRLF case if autocrlf was not true (the script marks that caveat).

title: paths and keys: registry keys and hub path_keys
proves: Registry keys use /; a case-insensitive collision of two keys falls back to ordinary sync; drive letters, UNC prefixes, and long paths (with core.longpaths) round-trip.
does_not_prove: NTFS 8.3 short names or Unicode normalization differences.

title: hub gate and checkpoint integration with a real repo
proves: The gate inside sync_all holds with a real repo; the checkpoint is written before the pointer flips; no code path renames a directory while it holds a handle in it; the unreadable-file test (an injected PermissionDenied, a skip and never a delete) passes on Windows. The injected error stands in for a real sharing violation; a real one needs a second process holding the file open.
does_not_prove: Network filesystems or Dev Drive behavior.
